'''''Resistance Reborn''''' is a [[canon]] novel written by [[Rebecca Roanhorse]]. It is part of the [[Journey to Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker|Journey to ''Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker'']] publishing program, and it was first published on [[November 5]], [[2019]] by [[Del Rey]], with an [[Resistance Reborn (audiobook)|audiobook]] version releasing on the same day. ''Resistance Reborn'' is set immediately after the events of the [[2017]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']], and it serves as a prequel to [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], illustrating the beginning of the [[Resistance]]'s way to regain military power by assembling allies, new leaders, pilots, and ships after the defeat at the [[Battle of Crait]].

{{Quote|So, what do we do now? We scatter to every corner of the galaxy, taking our message with us. We help those already fighting the First Order, we make allies, we sow the spark of Resistance. And when the time comes, we will be ready. We will rise up, and we will fight. And all of us, together, will burn the First Order to the ground.|[[Poe Dameron]]‘s first speech, outlining the future of the Resistance|<ref name="Resistance Reborn">''[[Resistance Reborn]]''</ref>}}
==Publisher's summary==
''The Resistance is in ruins. In the wake of their harrowing escape from Crait, what was once an army has been reduced to a handful of wounded heroes. Finn, Poe, Rey, Rose, Chewbacca, Leia Organa—their names are famous among the oppressed worlds they fight to liberate. But names can only get you so far, and Leia's last desperate call for aid has gone unanswered.''

''From the jungles of Ryloth to the shipyards of Corellia, the shadow of the First Order looms large, and those with the bravery to face the darkness are scattered and isolated. If hope is to survive, the Resistance must journey throughout the galaxy, seeking out more leaders—including those who, in days gone by, helped a nascent rebellion topple an empire. Battles will be fought, alliances will be forged, and the Resistance will be reborn.''

==Plot summary==

=== Death on Corellia ===
During the [[First Order]] [[Occupation of Corellia|occupation of]] [[Corellia]], a [[Resistance]] [[Resistance pilot|pilot]] from [[Doaba Guerfel]] flies a stolen [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE/ln space superiority fighter]] over [[Coronet City]] while under pursuit. Unable to contact the ''[[Raddus (MC85 Star Cruiser)|Raddus]]'' due to signal jamming, the pilot uploads a stolen encryption key, intended to prevent the construction of future superweapons, into her console. She tries to transmit the data to a contact of hers via an illegal radio frequency. Although the transmission puts the recipient at risk of First Order retaliation, the pilot successfully completes the transfer before her TIE fighter is destroyed by the pursuing ships. The pilot is killed in the explosion, which is witnessed by the citizens of the city below before they return to their daily lives.

=== Searching for allies ===
While aboard the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' following the [[Battle of Crait]], [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] suffers from recurring nightmares and physical exhaustion resulting from her recent exposure to the vacuum of space. Despite the ship's damaged subspace radio, she receives an encrypted transmission from [[Zay Versio]] and [[Shriv Suurgav]]. The pair reports that over half of the Resistance allies on Organa's list have vanished or abandoned their homes. Organa authorizes them to pursue leads involving former [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] personnel who oppose the [[First Order]], noting that the Resistance's dwindling options necessitate unconventional alliances.

[[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] provides Organa with [[Gatalentan tea]] from the ship's stores and the two discuss the loss of Resistance leadership, specifically [[Amilyn Holdo]] and [[Gial Ackbar]]. Organa emphasizes the need for strategists and inspirational figures to rebuild the movement. When Rey asks about the corruption of [[Ben Solo]], Organa states that her son must choose his own path to redemption. Rey also details her maintenance work on the ''Falcon's'' compressor, which sustained condensation damage due to the high humidity on [[Ahch-To]].

[[Poe Dameron]] later contacts the vessel to report that [[Black Squadron (Resistance)|Black Squadron]] has [[Battle of Ikkrukk|successfully defended]] [[Grail City]] on the planet [[Ikkrukk]]. While the mission resulted in zero Resistance casualties, pilots [[Jessika Pava]] and [[Suralinda Javos]] sustained minor injuries. Organa instructs Dameron to attend a function hosted by [[Prime Minister]] [[Grist]] to assess the guests' political loyalties and identify any separatist factions. She tasks him with securing a formal commitment of resources from Grist before ending the transmission and returning to her list of potential survivors.

On Ikkrukk, Black Squadron attends a celebratory function hosted by Grist in her [[Prime minister's cave palace|cave palace]]. During the event, Javos performs on a dais while Dameron attempts to secure military aid for the Resistance. Citing the fear of First Order retaliation and the need to repair planetary defenses, Grist refuses to formally join the Resistance, though she provides the squadron with fuel and food rations to facilitate their departure.

In private, [[Temmin Wexley|Temmin "Snap" Wexley]] and [[Karé Kun]] recount their recent failure on [[Pastoria]], where they were manipulated into assisting an unscrupulous faction during a civil war. Dameron then informs the squadron of the Resistance's near-total destruction during the [[Battle of D'Qar|evacuation of D'Qar]] and the [[Battle of Crait]], including [[Battle of Oetchi|the loss]] of [[Resistance navy|the fleet]] and his own role in the disastrous [[bombing run]]. Despite the high casualty rate and Dameron's demotion for insubordination, the pilots of Black Squadron choose to remain under his command.

Dameron assigns new objectives focused on recruiting veteran strategists to rebuild the movement. Wexley and Kun are dispatched to [[Akiva]] to recruit [[Wedge Antilles]] and [[Norra Wexley]]. Simultaneously, Javos and Pava are ordered to [[Rattatak]] to investigate rumors of a former Imperial official who has gained control over a local [[warlord]] faction. Dameron and [[BB-8]] depart on a mission to [[Ephemera]] seek assistance from fellow associate [[Maz Kanata]].

Dameron arrives over the [[Gas giant|gas planet]], specifically a tuusah spa in the capital city of [[Wish]]. He requests that Kanata provide the severely depleted Resistance with shelter, resources, and leadership. Kanata refuses to formally join the movement, citing [[Battle of Takodana|the destruction]] of [[Takodana Castle|her castle]] on [[Takodana]]. She challenges Dameron's arrogance, prompting him to confess his role in [[Battle of Oetchi|the mutiny aboard the Raddus]] and express remorse for his resulting leadership failures. Despite his plea, Kanata maintains her refusal, asserting that she fights the First Order in her own way.

As Dameron prepares to depart in his [[Unidentified starfighter|borrowed starfighter]], Kanata intercepts his vessel to share gathered intelligence. She reveals that the First Order has escalated its abduction operations, openly arresting and kidnapping individuals with ties to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]], as well as neutral or dissenting former Imperials. Kanata notes that these captives are primarily [[Death|executed]] or sent to [[Labor camp|labor camps]] to construct First Order military assets. She hypothesizes that this systemic purge accounts for the sudden disappearance of Leia Organa's allies. Finally, Kanata informs Dameron of a rumored master list detailing the abducted individuals and promises to contact the Resistance if her network locates it.

=== New directives ===
On Corellia, [[Winshur Bratt]], the First Order's executive records [[officer]] at the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation]], passes through security checkpoints while traveling to his office in Coronet City. Bratt, a former middle manager from [[Bela Vistal]], was retained and promoted by the First Order following their occupation of the shipyards. During his commute, he is confronted by a mechanic named [[Navah]], a former classmate who addresses him by a childhood nickname. Bratt dismisses her and continues to the [[Records Department]] in [[Building Two]].

Upon arrival, Bratt summons his assistants, [[Monti Calay]] and [[Yama Dex]]. He reprimands Yama for her non-regulation hairstyle and untidy uniform, delivering a lecture on the First Order's philosophy regarding discipline and power. Bratt instructs her to organize and label the mysterious tapes. When Yama drops a box while attempting to carry it out, Bratt refuses to assist her and informs her that the incident would be noted in her permanent disciplinary record. He then observes an interaction between Yama and Calay before returning to his duties, confident in his leadership and standing within the First Order.

On Akiva, Wedge and Norra live a quiet life as [[Farmer|farmers]] near the [[capital]] [[city]] of [[Myrra]]. While tending to his [[Keedee|daily chores]], Wedge observes two [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing starfighters]] landing on his property. Snap and Karé meet with Wedge and Norra inside their home to deliver news regarding the state of the galaxy. Snap informs them that the [[Resistance High Command|Resistance leadership]] had been devastated, with the deaths of Admiral Ackbar, Admiral Holdo, and [[Admiral]] [[Ushos O. Statura|Statura]]. He further revealed that [[Luke Skywalker]] had died during the conflict. This news leads Wedge to conclude that the First Order has effectively won [[First Order-Resistance War|the war]], suggesting that they will likely overlook Akiva due to its lack of strategic industry. Snap counters that the Resistance will live on as long as those willing to fight remain.

While Karé and Norra leave on a local errand to monitor First Order interest in the capital and repair their ship's weapons systems, Wedge and Snap remain at the homestead. Despite his desire for a quiet domestic life, Wedge admits that he cannot remain idle while the Resistance faces extinction. Although Norra  later expresses reservations about the high probability of death in the coming conflict, Wedge surreptitiously prepares a flight bag, having already committed to rejoin the fight.

Meanwhile, Bratt receives an urgent and confidential transmission from [[First Order High Command|First Order high command]]. The message contains three sensitive documents: a list of subversives, a list of individuals currently in First Order custody, and a specific list of fifteen high-profile prisoners being transferred to Corellia. His superior instructs him to bury the records in the archives and oversee the prisoners' integration into the shipyard labor pool under the guise of "reform through labor." Bratt is promised a promotion and a relocation to high command if he successfully manages the arrival and labor of these "Corellian Fifteen," which includes former diplomats and senators.

=== Mission to Ryloth ===
Aboard the ''Falcon'', Leia seeks assistance in replenishing the Resistance's depleted resources. Recalling her [[Bloodline (novel)|Senate-era investigation]] into the [[crime lord]] [[Rinnrivin Di]], Leia identifies [[Ryloth]] as a potential source of support. The ''Falcon'' is forced to make an emergency jump to the [[Ryloth system]] due to critical fuel shortages, arriving without clearance. Upon exiting hyperspace, the ''Falcon'' is intercepted by [[Lessu command|Lessu government]] [[Starfighter|fighters]]. Rey attempts to obscure the ship's identity by using the pseudonym "Pilot Rey of the Han System" and claiming to carry medical supplies. The situation is de-escalated when a stealth [[Rycrit-class]] vessel, identifying itself as [[RDA One]], overrides the local authorities. The pilot of the stealth ship utilizes a secured Resistance frequency to lead the ''Falcon'' to a hidden facility that serves as the headquarters for the [[Ryloth Defense Authority]]. Leia and the Resistance are greeted by [[Hahnee Brethen]] and [[Ambassador]] [[Charth Brethen]]. Despite the RDA's desire for anonymity, the group is granted an audience with the organization's leader, [[Yendor Brethen]], a former [[rebel pilot]] and associate of Organa. During a private meeting on the facility's balcony, Leia requests sanctuary and logistical support for the Resistance's remaining forces. Yendor initially hesitates, citing Ryloth's hard-won neutrality and the risk of First Order retaliation. Charth Brethen further notes that the RDA lacks the capacity to house a large military force. However, Organa reveals that the Resistance had been reduced to those in the ''Falcon'' and a handful of pilots. Moved by the scale of the loss and his personal history with Organa, Yendor agrees to provide aid, effectively aligning the RDA with the Resistance.

=== [[Escape from Akiva]] ===
On Akiva, Wedge and Norra are alerted to the presence of an armed security detail in their yard. Suspecting the group to be First Order [[Operative|operatives]] investigating their X-wings, the couple decides to evacuate the planet and rejoin the Resistance. While Snap and Karé utilize an underground tunnel to reach the starfighters with the group's gear, Wedge and Norra attemp a distraction. Dressed in civilian robes over their flight suits to appear as harmless farmers, the couple exits their home and are immediately intercepted by three armed guards. Their neighbor, [[Tukalda]], identifies Norra as a former member of the Rebel Alliance, leading to a firefight in which the guards are killed and Tukalda is incapacitated. Norra and Wedge hide the bodies and flee the planet in a stolen leisure shuttle to rendezvous with Snap and Karé.

=== Rebuilding the Resistance ===
Meanwhile, Poe departs Ephemera and receives coordinates for a temporary Resistance base on a [[Ryloth's third moon|moon of Ryloth]] from [[Rose Tico]]. Poe coordinates with his various teams via comms, confirming [[Escape from Akiva|the successful extraction of Wedge and Norra]]. Jess and Suralinda are trying to recruit ex-Imperial strategist [[Teza Nasz]] through gladiatorial combat, while Shriv Suurgav and [[Inferno Squad (Resistance)|Inferno Squadron]] secure other allies.

On Ryloth, General Leia Organa remains aboard the ''Falcon'' while Yendor informs her that a First Order diplomatic mission has arrived in [[Lessu City]] to demand taxes from the shipping guild. To offset recent military losses, the First Order is demanding immediate taxes from the Ryloth shipping guild. They have issued a five-day ultimatum before enforcing a total planetary blockade. Yendor warns Leia that [[Chancellor]] [[Drelomon]], desperate to avoid conflict, may betray the Resistance if he discovers their presence. This shrinks the Resistance's window of opportunity to gather allies and escape to less than five days. During the [[Twi'lek]] [[Holiday (disambiguation)|holiday]] of the [[Longest Night]], the Resistance fleet, consisting of ten X-wings, an [[A-wing starfighter|A-wing]], a borrowed Hutt starfighter, two civilian transports, and a [[luxury yacht]], arrives at a hidden hangar in the southern desert.

Leia, accompanied by a mourning R2-D2 (who has just completed repairs on the Falcon alongside Rey), greets the arrivals. Poe introduces several vital new assets to the understaffed movement. [[Carlist Rieekan]]'s reunion with Leia brings immense emotional relief. [[Orrimaarko]], a [[Dressellian]] battle strategist and veteran of the Battle of Endor, is also present. As the factions mingle, a physical altercation breaks out in the hangar between Nasz and a young pilot named [[Pacer Agoyo]], cutting the introductions short.

Poe arrives to find Agoyo wearing a [[Phantom Squadron]] uniform belonging to [[Pacer Agoyo's father|his late father]]. Nasz defeats an ally of Agoyo's, leaving the [[pilot]] sliding across the floor in a streak of [[blood]]. When Agoyo accuses Nasz of murdering his [[Pacer Agoyo's brother|brother]], Poe defuses the situation by threatening to place Agoyo in the [[brig]], while Wedge pulls the enraged young pilot back. Nasz admits she likely killed many of relatives during her Imperial service because she mistakenly believed it was right at the time. Poe uses the moment to unify the gathering by highlighting that many present have complex pasts, citing Wedge's time at [[Skystrike Academy]], Zay Versio's Imperial [[Desertion|defecting]] [[Parent|parents]], Suralinda's past attempt to sell Resistance secrets, and Finn's history as a [[First Order stormtrooper]]. [[Sanrec Stronghammer]] then challenges Poe directly, demanding accountability for his insubordination and mutiny against Holdo. Poe acknowledges his failures and expresses deep remorse, which prompts supportive testimonials from Karé, Jess, and Finn. Zay assists Poe in concluding his speech with a unified call for the faction to choose to be better.

Following the resolution of the conflict, Leia convenes her newly established leadership council, consisting of Poe, Wedge, Stronghammer, Nasz, Rieekan, Orrimaarko, Norra, Snap, Shriv, Charth, and the crew of the Falcon for a briefing in Yendor's [[library]], which has been converted into a tactical war room. Stronghammer establishes a rapport with Poe, wagering that he can outrace him if they can secure a U-wing, with the loser agreeing to shave their hair to match Stronghammer's look. During the briefing, Leia confirms that the First Order has successfully [[Frequency jammer|blocked]] standard communication frequencies and is actively capturing Resistance allies across the galaxy. Charth details the First Order's economic leverage over Ryloth's shipping lanes to finance their naval reconstruction. To combat their severe resource deficit, Dameron advocates for a raid on the Corellian shipyards to secure starfighters. Shriv suggests targeting [[Bracca]] instead, noting that the First Order is now using the junker world to decommission captured New Republic vessels, making it a viable source for starships and replacement components. Connix interrupts the session to patch through an urgent encrypted holographic transmission from Maz.

Maz reveals that an associate named [[Nifera Shu]] has obtained a stolen and encrypted First Order data file listing political dissidents and prisoners. Nifera intends to sell the file to the highest bidder at an invitation-only auction hosted during her birthday party in Coronet City. Maz secures two invitations for the event: one for the ambassador of Ryloth and a guest, and another for a fictional high-rolling profiteer from [[Canto Bight]] and his business partner. She transmits the partial data file to the war room, which materializes as a hologram bearing the sixteen-rayed hexagon [[First Order insignia|insignia of the First Order]].

The transmitted data contains two separate lists. The first list, under the heading SUBVERSIVES, features scrambled names of individuals targeted for assassination, including a set of initials matching Dameron linked to his last known location on Crait, as well as entries associated with [[Castilon]]. The second list, titled CURRENTLY DETAINED, logs encrypted initials of high-profile captives alongside their official convictions for minor offenses against [[Supreme Leader]] [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]]. Nasz notes the expansive scope of the First Order's sweeps, which include civilian figures like grav-ball champion Cutar Har.

Leia identifies a specific entry on the detainee list located in Coronet City: a senator designated by the initials "R. C." convicted of conspiracy and crimes against the state. Recognizing the entry as her former ally [[Ransolm Casterfo]], whom she previously believed had been executed, Leia authorizes a multi-pronged offensive. The strategy is divided into three distinct operations: Shriv commands the salvage team to Bracca alongside Zay, Agoyo, and Stronghammer; Poe coordinates the infiltration of the auction in Coronet City alongside Charth to secure the master list; Wedge and Norra organize a tactical team to locate and extract Casterfo from the Corellian detention site. Leia, Rieekan, and Yendor remain on Ryloth to provide remote tactical oversight despite the active First Order presence in the system.

=== A bureaucratic trap ===
On Corellia, Winshur oversees the secret arrival of high-profile New Republic political prisoners. Supervised by First Order reform officer [[Colonel]] [[Genial]], He assigns the captives to brutal labor details. [[Hevasi Joy]], a famous anti-First Order protest [[Musician|singer]], is assigned to [[Janitor|sanitation]]. [[Ransolm Casterfo]], a notorious former New Republic senator previously believed to have been executed for political assassination, is assigned to a deadly sewage pipe fitting detail in the shipyards, a role with a high mortality rate due to lethal gas leaks.

The following day, Winshur is ambushed in his office by [[Hasadar Shu]], a wealthy Corellian businessman, who claims a fabricated personal history with Winshur, accurately naming his hometown and his mother. Shu arrives alongside Genial. Left with no graceful exit, a paranoid Winshur is coerced into a future business luncheon. While Winshur is on break, Monti steals his [[datapad]], which contains the encrypted master prisoner list. Motivated by a sudden moral awakening after witnessing the broken prisoners, he then flees to a [[cantina]] called the [[Dead Aeronaut]]. There, he meets a slicer from [[Collective|The Collective]], an underground tech network opposed to authoritarianism. The contact, wearing facial-recognition-blocking makeup and a white scarf, confirms that the Collective possesses the decryption key.

While the slicer copies the data in the restroom, [[Corellian Security Forces|CorSec]] [[Guard|guards]] raid the cantina searching for a slicer. Utilizing a haughty, arrogant persona modeled after his boss, Monti successfully bluffs the guards, explaining away his suspicious double order of salted squid by leveraging his First Order authority. The guards inspect the restroom only to find it completely empty; the slicer has escaped through a small window with the stolen satchel. Though initially terrified of being executed for losing the device, Monti is stopped by the [[bartender]], [[Smokey (bartender)|Smokey]], who returns the satchel. The Collective agent successfully extracted the data and covertly slipped the physical datapad back into Monti's bag, leaving him safe from immediate detection.

While attempting to return the datapad to Winshur's office, Monti is confronted by Yama. He attempts to deflect her suspicion by claiming he is tidying the office and feigning an illness, but Yama draws a box cutter and accuses him of theft. To defuse the threat, Monti points out that the datapad is still on the desk and challenges her to report him, noting that Winshur's contempt for her ensures his superiors will not believe her story. When Winshur returns to the office, he reprimands Yama for blocking his path with supplies and ignoring her duties. Noticing Monti's sweating, he then fears contagion and orders him to go home. Exploiting the distraction, Monti teases Yama a final time and permanently abandons his position.

=== [[Mission to Bracca]] ===
Shriv, Zay, Agoyo, Stronghammer, along with wives [[Wesson Dove]] and [[Raidah Doon]], depart Ryloth for Bracca to salvage decommissioned New Republic starships. Operating as [[Dross Squadron]], the group plans to infiltrate the [[Scrapper Guild]] by posing as a replacement [[Hazmat (occupation)|Hazmat crew]] arranged by Agoyo's sister. Upon arriving in orbit, Shriv orders Versio to remain behind as the transport's pilot and a safety backup for the ground team.

The remaining operatives board a [[Monorail|monorail transport train]] to Platform 33. During the transit, a squad of First Order stormtroopers boards the car. Agoyo, whose family home was destroyed by the First Order, attempts to attack them, but Shriv intervenes and enforces the chain of command to protect the mission. Upon disembarking at the platform, the group is halted by the stormtroopers after Raidah's facial features trigger a criminal alert for a past theft on [[Gheia Six]]. A First Order officer arrives and orders the detention of the entire crew for collusion. Before the guards can secure them, Wesson kills the officer with a concealed knife, initiating a firefight in the terminal.

As Dross Squadron scrambles for cover, they are pinned down by suppressive fire, forcing them to adopt a defensive posture amidst the open-platform environment. Wesson is struck by a blaster bolt to the ribs while Sanrec sustains a grievous shot to his lower leg, rendering him unable to maneuver effectively. The tide of the shootout shifts with the arrival of a local guild Scrapper unit, which is led by a combatant named [[Puwanini]].

=== Crossing the Ibdis Maw ===
To reach the platform where the starfighters are held, Dross Squadron is forced to traverse over a dangerous creature known as the [[Ibdis Maw]]. Recognizing the inability to physically cross the the Maw, the Scrappers improvise a transit solution, utilizing thruster-packs and tension cables to propel themselves across the abyss. Sanrec, however, concludes that he cannot safely make the transit across the Maw due to his weight and injured leg. Utilizing a seized blaster to engage the pursuing stormtroopers, Stronghammer's act of defiance allows the remaining members of Dross Squadron, including the critically wounded Wesson, to evacuate.

Upon arriving at the designated platform, the survivors discover a significant, albeit incomplete, cache of starfighters, including several [[T-70 X-wing starfighter|T-70 X-wing starfighters]], a [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]], and a highly advanced [[T-85 X-wing starfighter]]. The extraction mission quickly becomes a race against time when the First Order, realizing the intent of the intruders, initiates a tilt maneuver on the landing platform to dump the starfighters into the Ibdis Maw. The team is forced to link the crippled starfighters together using scavenged cabling to be towed by the few functional vessels. The Resistance crew is saved only by the intervention of Dross Squadron's original transport vessel, which arrives under the command of Zay. Utlizing the transport's defensive weaponry, she suppresses the First Order's [[heavy repeater cannon]] fire, allowing the stolen crafts to break orbit.

=== Preperations and deployment ===
Poe finds Finn and Rey huddled in close conversation on a bunk within the Falcon. Rey speaks in a hurried whisper until Poe clears his throat, causing her to jump. She exits the quarters, despite Finn's attempt to call her back. Poe apologizes for the interruption. Finn clarifies that his relationship with Rey is platonic, and confirms a similar platonic understanding exists between himself and Rose. Poe then offers Finn an invitation to join [[Corellian Team One]], the group of spies sent to infiltrate Nifera's auction. Finn enthusiastically accepts the assignment to escape the monotony of counting supplies and rations, comparing the administrative chores unfavorably to his past sanitation duties on Starkiller Base.

On the way across the hangar, Finn notes that Rey went to brief Leia on their prior discussion. Poe expresses concern for Leia's safety, but Finn remains confident in Rey's capabilities. Poe outlines the immediate plan to transit to Corellia and infiltrate the shipyards. At the transport, Charth appears dressed in high-quality formal attire and explains he recruited Suralinda for the mission as well. Suralinda then approaches wearing a [[silk]] dress obtained from the historical clothing wing of the base. She carries additional formal wardrobe pieces for Poe and Finn.

Poe receives the alias of Lorell Shda, a notorious weapons dealer seeking to liberate captured comrades, while Finn takes the identity of his business partner, [[Kade Genti]], a name derived from [[Kade Genti, Master of Section Nine|an old Coruscant entertainment feed comic book]] smuggled to him by stormtrooper [[FN-1971]] during their youth. Charth urges an immediate departure as time grows short. Finn jokes about his history of being arrested at high-society events, prompting Suralinda to toast to a potential blaze of glory. Poe sharpens his tone, reminding the team that survival is the primary objective to ensure the future of the Resistance. Charth notes quietly that death can claim anyone regardless of effort. Poe assists Finn with his tie, acknowledging his decision to wear an Alliance starbird pin found on Crait, and the team departs.

At the same time, [[Corellian Team Two]] loads an [[Imperial shuttle]] for a rescue [[mission to Corellia]]. Wedge and Norra discuss Casterfo. Leia believes he is the high-profile captive listed under the initials "R. C." in a decrypted First Order file. Snap and Karé express skepticism regarding Casterfo's survival, but Nasz explains that the First Order prefers lifetime imprisonment over creating political martyrs. Despite Snap's reluctance to include Nasz, Antilles notes her knowledge of Imperial security architecture is necessary to infiltrate Coronet City cleanly.

=== Corporate crisis ===
An exhausted Winshur returns to his office from the luncheon with Hasadar, finding Yama sleeping at her desk. In a fit of irrational rage, he assaults his employee. Shortly after, Winshur retreats to the restroom and is cornered by Genial, who reveals that Yama reported Monti for the theft of the datapad. He claims that Monti is connected to a conspiracy surrounding the upcoming Shu auction. Manipulating Winshur's fear and confusion, Genial asserts that he is ultimately responsible for the breach and will face severe consequences. Terrified, Winshur agrees to assist Genial in retrieving the list from the auction in exchange for a potential plea for mercy.

Later, Wedge, Norra, Snap, and Nasz arrive at the occupied shipyards. The team encounters a young First Order cadet in a restricted area. When the cadet demands identification, Nasz quickly incapacitates him to maintain their cover. The group proceeds into a facility, observing that it functions largely as a museum for shipbuilding history, before navigating to the executive records office. Inside, Wedge, Norra, Snap, and Nasz discover a severely beaten Yama Dex. Utilizing her [[eidetic memory]], Yama confirms that the prisoner the Resistance is seeking, Prisoner 876549C, is Ransolm Casterfo.

Empowered, Nasz successfully decrypts Winshur's datapad, discovering that Casterfo is currently assigned to sewage detail and is being housed in [[Dormitory F]], a section of the facility used as a covert prison block. Yama guides the Resistance fighters through the facility's skytowers after they dispatch the guards stationed at the entrance.

While the rest of the team conducts a tense, door-to-door search for their allies, Nasz locates the warden's office and deliberately triggers an emergency alarm to unlock every cell door in the building. As confused and wary captives emerge into the halls, Wedge successfully locates a weary and battered Casterfo. Though the former senator initially claims his name is a curse, Wedge assures him that Leia Organa sent them, successfully recruiting Casterfo to the Resistance.

=== Assault on Yendor's library ===
Simultaneously, on Ryloth, Leia and Rey convene in Yendor's library to monitor ongoing missions. Rey, experiencing a premonition of danger, expresses growing unease regarding the safety of the Resistance. Her fears are validated when a proximity [[Alarm system|alarm]] sounds, signaling that the First Order has tracked the Resistance to their location. As the library's defensive shutters engage, Yendor orders a full-scale alert, confirming that the facility is under attack.

=== The Shu Auction ===
Upon arriving at Nifera's auction, Poe and Finn encounter First Order security forces. Despite a tense moment where a stormtrooper recognizes Poe, the pair successfully clears the checkpoint using fabricated identities and a diversionary story about Poe's fame at a [[fathier]] track. They reach the party, an elaborate underwater-themed event, and present their gift to Nifera and her husband, revealed to be Hasadar: a [[lylek]] queen in a cage. Nifera accepts the unusual gift with enthusiasm, providing Dameron with a packet containing an imagecaster and an earpiece, advising him to let the Force guide his efforts before the "games" begin at five minutes past the hour.

After regrouping with Suralinda and Charth, Poe and Finn retreat to a balcony to access the auction. Using the provided gear, Poe logs into an encrypted auction interface hosted by the Collective. Upon connecting, the system automatically seizes 50% of the Resistance's credits as a non-refundable "donation." Despite Poe's efforts, the prices escalate rapidly, and the Resistance's depleted funds are quickly exhausted. When they fail to supply additional credits, the system issues a self-destruct warning, forcing Poe to disconnect. Realizing the auction requires the winner to be physically present to claim the list, Poe concludes that the auction itself may be a misdirection.

Before the Resistance can attempt to acquire the list through other means, the auction is attacked by a contingent of stormtroopers. One of the First Order officers declares the gathering illegal and orders the arrest of all guests. When Hasadar steps forward to protest the raid on his private residence, the lead stormtrooper fires at his head. The subsequent collapse of a banquet table triggers panic, leading the stormtroopers to fire into the crowd as chaos erupts.

Charth escapes to prepare the Resistance ship for extraction, but as he does, Poe, Finn, and Suralinda spot Nifera attempting to flee the violence. Knowing that she possesses the master list, Poe corners her on a balcony, reveals his Resistance affiliation, and offers her safe passage off-world in exchange for the intelligence. Nifera retrieves a hidden datachip from the mouth of her pet horned eel and agrees to the terms. To evade the rapidly advancing First Order troops, Poe and Nifera leap from the balcony into a dark ornamental pool. They survive the drop and are pulled ashore by Finn and Suralinda. However, the group soon learns from Charth that their ship has been entirely surrounded by stormtroopers, effectively trapping them on the estate grounds.

Seeking an alternative escape route, Finn suggests contacting Wedge. Suralinda contacts Connix to obtain Corellian Team Two's current coordinates, learning in the process that the Resistance forces at the Ryloth base are facing an emergency evacuation.

Meanwhile, at the CEC campus, Snap receives an urgent communication from Karé, who reports that Poe's squad has lost their ship and is now stranded. Despite the massive challenge of transporting any and all willing prisoners and the looming threat of First Order reinforcements, Wedge refuses to leave anyone behind, ordering Poe to rendezvous so they can escape Corellia together. Poe's team, encouraged, sets out into Coronet City.

=== Bratt's resolution ===
Elsewhere, Winshur and Genial travel on foot toward the wealthy district to oversee the detention of Hasadar Shu. As they cross a high bridge over a vast inland sea channel, Genial relentlessly berates Winshur, accusing the records officer of treason and threatening him with a merciless execution. Instead of cowering, Bratt experiences a sudden psychological fracture and subsequent shift, realizing his unwavering ideological loyalty to the First Order and wholly rejecting Genial's accusations.

Hearing the sounds of blaster fire and screams erupting from the Shu estate, Genial orders Winshur to hurry so they can witness the arrests. Empowered by his newfound, violent resolve, Winshur sprints toward the colonel and unexpectedly tackles him over the bridge's railing. Genial plummets into the icy, dark waters below and does not resurface. Standing alone on the bridge, Winshur descends into a hysterical fit of laughter, feeling completely liberated from his previous anxieties and fears. Rationalizing the murder as a necessary choice for his own survival, he decides to hunt down Monti and frame her as a Resistance traitor. Embracing his newly ruthless persona, Winshur races back to his office.

At the campus, Bratt spots Yama and tails her into a dimly lit maintenance passage with the intent to kill the teenager. When he corners his rogue assistant, she attempts to defend herself with a metal pipe, confronting Bratt about his abusive behavior and hypocritical claims of discipline. A brief physical struggle ensues, resulting in Bratt overpowering the girl and seizing her makeshift weapon. Just as Yama's boss prepares to strike a fatal blow, he is interrupted by Tesa Nasz. Unfazed by Bratt's arrogance and refusal to back down, the former Imperial warlord casually shoots the records officer in the stomach with her blaster, neutralizing the threat and rescuing Yama before continuing the evacuation.

Fatally wounded, Bratt lies bleeding on the cold concrete as the fleeing Resistance team and their newly liberated prisoners walk past him toward their extraction point. Ransolm Casterfo momentarily pauses to offer the dying officer a gesture of pity, but a humiliated Bratt rolls over to face the wall, refusing to accept mercy. Left alone in his final moments, Bratt is forced to realize that the violence and authoritarian power he worshipped have ultimately betrayed and destroyed him.

=== Escape from Ryloth ===
During the First Order assault on the RDA's hidden hangar, the Resistance struggles to hold off the advancing forces and evacuate their personnel. Leia  fights alongside Rey to cover the retreat after Hahnee is killed in the initial battle. The Resistance forces manage to fall back and board their respective ships, though Leia is enraged by the political betrayal from the capital city of Lessu that led to the devastating ambush. She contacts Yendor, who is holding the south end of the hangar, to inform him of his daughter's death. Grief-stricken, Yendor plans to stay behind and man a hidden surface-to-air cannon to cover the Resistance's escape. He instructs Leia to tell his grandchildren that he died defending a free Ryloth. However, when Leia informs him that Phantom Squadron is short a pilot, Yendor changes his mind and rushes to fly the vacant X-wing. Aboard the Falcon, Leia, Rey, and the surviving fleet break through the atmosphere, reaffirming their shared belief that the Resistance can preserve the hope needed to eventually defeat the First Order.

=== The Battle of Corellia ===
On Corellia, Wedge's team navigates the blaring alarms of the CEC campus alongside their rescued prisoners. They successfully rendezvous with Poe, who has secured Nifera and the master list of abducted allies. Facing a blockade of over sixty stormtroopers guarding the shipyard hangars, Wedge and Norra  volunteer to create a diversion. They draw the enemy's fire so that the rest of the Resistance operatives can successfully escort the weakened prisoners to a stolen shuttle.

The diversion succeeds in splitting the First Order forces, allowing Snap and the others to reach the transports. However, Wedge and Norra are quickly pinned down behind makeshift cover, and Wedge sustains a severe blaster wound to his right arm. Refusing to abandon her husband, Norra prepares for a final stand against the advancing stormtroopers. Just as they face certain death, Poe arrives in a starfighter and blasts the interior wall of the building, obliterating the remaining enemy forces. Surviving the collapse, Wedge and Norra safely board the craft, where Snap emotionally addresses Wedge as his father before the Resistance safely evacuates the planet.

=== A scattered spark ===
Following their successful extraction from the Corellian Engineering Corporation, Poe leads the Resistance forces out of Corellia's atmosphere aboard a stolen First Order shuttle and a [[CR90 corvette]]. Under pursuit, Suralinda breaks off to run interference while Karé relays grim news from Ryloth: Leia and the Millennium Falcon have survived the First Order ambush, but several allies have perished. With nowhere safe to jump, Poe negotiates with Nifera, who agrees to provide coordinates to a Collective safe house in exchange for the remainder of the Resistance's financial assets.

Arriving at the secret Collective facility, Poe and Finn smuggle the liberated prisoners, including Ransolm Casterfo, into the hidden base. Casterfo shares an emotional reunion with Leia, who has already begun disseminating the master list of abducted allies with Yendor and Orrimaarko to coordinate rescue and recruitment efforts. Realizing that congregating in one location makes the group highly vulnerable to the First Order, Poe addresses the assembled Resistance fighters and declares a new strategy. He orders the movement to scatter across the galaxy to build alliances, assist localized rebellions, and ignite the spark of resistance everywhere.

Embracing their role in the decentralized rebellion, Wedge and Norra bid an emotional farewell to Snap, choosing to return to the stars as pilots rather than military leaders. As the various factions prepare to disperse and carry out their new mission, Rey and Finn eagerly join Poe's team. Observing the young leaders, Leia watches with silent satisfaction, confident that the future of the Resistance is finally in capable hands.
